goal: A highly polished, responsive browser-based decision board styled as a private strategy atelier. Small teams can add options, score them from 1 to 5 across customizable criteria, view a deterministic leader, and persist their sessions locally. The interface features a calm, editorial layout with warm parchment backgrounds, charcoal ink typography, restrained brass accents, and subtle tactile depth.
constraints: Strictly offline: no external CDNs, packages, or network calls
Only five files: index.html, styles.css, app.js, journey.json, README.md
Vanilla JS, HTML, CSS, and inline SVGs only
Must fit within a $3.00 budget and 20-minute execution window
Exclusion or preservation: No external CSS or JS frameworks (Tailwind, Bootstrap, React, etc.)
Exclusion or preservation: No external icon libraries or web fonts
Exclusion or preservation: No server-side databases or user authentication

Approved visual direction: Calm editorial layout inspired by a private strategy atelier. Warm parchment background (#FDFBF7), charcoal ink text (#1C1A17), restrained brass accents (#C5A059), strong typographic hierarchy using system serif headers, subtle tactile borders, and purposeful micro-interactions.
Operating context: Modern desktop and mobile browsers (Chromium, Safari, Firefox)
Operating context: Fully offline-capable, zero network dependencies
acceptance_criteria: Users can add, edit, and remove decision options
Users can score options from 1 to 5 across multiple criteria
A deterministic leader is calculated and highlighted in real-time
Data persists automatically to LocalStorage and can be cleared after confirmation
The UI matches the 'private strategy atelier' aesthetic (parchment, charcoal, brass)
The application is fully keyboard-accessible and responsive
Deterministic leader calculation with clear tie-breaking logic
Confirmation dialogs before clearing or resetting board data
Zero console errors during standard user journey
Responsive layout that adapts seamlessly from mobile screens to wide desktop monitors
